description:
## Symptom, minimized to nine lines

    defmodule My do
      @spec rev([a], [a]) :: [a]
      fn rev([], tail), do: tail
      fn rev([h | t], acc), do: rev(t, [h | acc])
    end

    fn main() do
      acc = My.rev([1, 2, 3], [])
      dbg(acc)                  # [3, 2, 1]   correct
      dbg(My.rev(acc, []))      # []          WRONG -- Elixir: [1, 2, 3]
    end

No protocol, no closure, no Enum, no Range. `fz2 interp`, `fz2 run` (JIT) and
`fz2 build` (AOT) all print `[3, 2, 1]` then `[]`.

`List.reverse/2` in the runtime library is exactly this function with exactly
this spec, so the four-line user-facing form is:

    fn main() do
      acc = List.reverse([1, 2, 3], [])
      dbg(acc)                     # [3, 2, 1]
      dbg(List.reverse(acc, []))   # []   -- Elixir Enum.reverse/2: [1, 2, 3]
    end

## The isolating differential: it is the SHARED SPEC VARIABLE

Same body, same call sites, only the `@spec` changes:

    @spec rev([a], [a]) :: [a]          -> [] .... WRONG
    @spec rev([a], [b]) :: [a]          -> [1,2,3]  correct
    @spec rev([a], [a]) :: any          -> [] .... WRONG   (return position is irrelevant)
    @spec rev([integer], [integer]) :: [integer]  -> [1,2,3]  correct
    (no @spec at all)                   -> [1,2,3]  correct

One type variable named in TWO parameter positions is the entire trigger.
Renaming the second to `b` fixes it. Making both concrete fixes it. Deleting
the spec fixes it. The result position does not participate.

## What the compiler actually does (--dump activations)

Correct build (`[a], [b]`) -- one activation:

    My.rev/2[[int], [a1_e]]
      @... => My.rev/2([int], [int]) => [int]
      @... => My.rev/2([int], [])    => [int]
      @... => My.rev/2([int], [])    => [int]

Broken build (`[a], [a]`) -- a SECOND, degenerate activation appears and the
self-composing call site binds to it:

    My.rev/2[[], [a1_e]]        <-- phantom: first parameter is the EMPTY LIST
    My.rev/2[[int], [a1_e]]
      @... => My.rev/2([int], [int]) => [int]
      @... => My.rev/2([int], [])    => [int]
      @... => My.rev/2([],   [])     => []      <-- the wrong answer, typed in

The wrong answer is not a codegen slip. The compiler has CONCLUDED that the
second call's list argument is the empty list, specialized `rev` to the
empty-list case where the only reachable clause is `rev([], tail), do: tail`,
and correctly returned that clause's `tail`, which is `[]`. The runtime is
faithfully executing a wrong fact.

## Why it is sometimes loud instead of silent

Remove the intermediate `dbg(acc)` and the same program fails hard:

    fn main() do
      dbg(List.reverse(List.reverse([1, 2, 3], []), []))
    end
    => fz2 interp: backend value 1 is unbound

Same defect. The empty-typed argument makes the value look dead, so transport
never materializes it; the `dbg` forces materialization and converts the crash
into a wrong answer.

## Falsified hypotheses (do not re-run these)

- "The first call's empty `[]` tail poisons the second." FALSIFIED: giving the
  first call a non-empty tail (`List.reverse([1,2,3], [0])`) still produces
  `[]`.
- "The second argument being provably non-empty avoids it." FALSIFIED:
  `List.reverse([9 | acc], [])` -- an argument that cannot be the empty list --
  is STILL typed `([], [])`.
- "Shared spec variables meet instead of join, per call." FALSIFIED for the
  non-recursive case: `@spec pick(a, a) :: a` / `fn pick(x, _y), do: x` called
  as `My.pick(1, :ok)` types cleanly as `My.pick/2(int, :ok) => int`. The
  defect needs RECURSION plus the shared variable plus a second call that
  consumes the first call's result.

## Provenance

Pre-existing. NOT a regression from the fz-km1/fz-qe0/fz-zg4/fz-6gb/
fz-f98.14.11/fz-06a stack: reproduced byte-identically at the stack base
6203da681 (fz-66j, PR #89) in a clean detached worktree.

## Why P1

A silent wrong answer, on every backend, for a nine-line program, from a
correct `@spec` on a textbook recursive accumulator. It is the only defect in
the fz-f98 epic that ships bad data rather than failing to compile.

## Where to start

The phantom `My.rev/2[[], [a1_e]]` is minted while the shared variable still
has no evidence -- `[a]` with `a` unresolved degenerates to the empty-list
type rather than staying an uninstantiated variable ([[unknown-is-not-none]]).
Confirm that first, at the earliest fact that names `[[], [a1_e]]`, before
touching refinement or transport. `refine_contract_inputs` (semantic.rs:1666)
keeps a narrowed argument whenever the intersection is non-empty, and
`intersect([int], [])` is the non-empty `[]`, so a degenerate surface silently
narrows a good argument instead of tripping the empty-intersection fallback --
but that is the propagation path, not necessarily the mint site.

## Relation to fz-f98.10 and the live enum_take_drop_split reds

`Enum.drop_while` is `drop_while_finish(reduce_while(..., {[], true}, ...))`
and its finish step reverses the accumulated list, so this shape sits directly
under the failing fixture. Shared root is UNPROVEN and must not be assumed.
fz-f98.10's own separate differential (swapping `List.reduce_while` for
`Enum.reduce_while` in an otherwise identical program) points at the protocol
callback hop, which this ticket does not involve at all.

## Checks

- The nine-line `My.rev` program prints `[3, 2, 1]` then `[1, 2, 3]` on interp,
  run and build, and its activation census contains no `[[], ...]` activation.
- The four-line `List.reverse` form agrees with its Elixir oracle.
- `dbg(List.reverse(List.reverse([1,2,3], []), []))` prints `[1, 2, 3]` with no
  unbound backend value.
- A lib regression test pins the shared-spec-variable shape at the layer that
  mints the degenerate activation.
- Full lib + matrix at baseline.

comments.text:
RESOLVED by commit 7a69440b7, PR #96 (draft, based on fz-06a/envelope-only-tested-slots).

ROOT CAUSE, confirmed at the calculator: Types::match_arrow dropped
empty-list-ambiguous variables from the WHOLE match instead of from the
position that observed the []. `([a], [a])` applied to `([int], [])` pins
a = int at parameter 1 and learns nothing at parameter 2; the global veto threw
parameter 1's proof away, [a] stayed a free variable, and instantiating a free
variable in list position yields []. refine_contract_inputs then narrowed the
caller's good [int] argument against that [] and KEPT it, because its
empty-intersection fallback does not fire -- [] is not the empty type, it is an
inhabited type with one value.

FIX: collect the substitution one position at a time, clean it there, union it
in. Ambiguity is a property of the witness, not of the variable. This DELETES
the match-wide ambiguous_vars/ambiguous_seen sets and the surface_sigma filter
(two call sites) rather than adding a rule -- union-on-rebind already did the
right thing once the noise never entered. Net -19 lines of mechanism, +1
six-line helper. A variable every position leaves ambiguous still never enters
the substitution, so the pre-existing empty_list_binding_is_ambiguous test
(`f(a) :: a` applied to []) passes unchanged.

TESTS (both proven red with the fix reverted, then restored):
- compiler2::types::arrow_match::tests::empty_list_position_does_not_veto_a_variable_another_position_pins
  (without the fix: Underconstrained { params: [[a], [a]] })
- fixtures2/behavior/spec_shared_var_self_composition, all 3 lanes
  (interp/run/build), golden owned by its Elixir oracle. Covers both
  List.reverse/2 and a user-written My.rev/2 with the same spec, so it holds
  even if the runtime library stops spelling reverse this way. fz and Elixir
  agree line for line.

GATES: lib 1443 passed / 4 failed (was 1442/4 -- same 4 inherited
enum_take_drop_split reds, +1 new test); matrix 410 passed / 3 failed (was
407/3 -- same 3 inherited, +3 new lanes); clippy --workspace --all-targets
clean; fmt clean.

SCOPE: does NOT close enum_take_drop_split. Verified after the fix -- the
fixture fails with the identical message (`public closure callsite 0 settled
return ... disagrees with its semantic result type \`any\``). That residual is
fz-f98.10's protocol-callback hop, which this change does not touch.

DOCS: .agent/docs/addressed-arrow.md behavior 5 rewritten -- ambiguity is a
property of the witness, why the substitution is per-position, and why the
global veto was wrong.

NOTE: no scaffolding or affordances added; nothing to schedule for removal.

title: A recursive fn whose @spec shares one type variable across two parameters mints a degenerate empty activation on self-composition (silent wrong answer, all three backends)
